correctness.rationale: Zeckendorf uniqueness makes the Fibonacci cutoff exactly a path of L available indices 2 through L+1. The ordered transfer product for a full period followed by the partial period has constant block P(0) idempotent of rank one, so the truncated inverse of det(I-tP)=1-t+O(y) has, in y-degree s, denominator dividing (1-t)^(s+1). This gives an eventual degree-at-most-s polynomial in q at each residue. In full blocks the unrestricted subset product has logarithm q(y A_s-y^2 B_s/2+O(y^3)); its repeated-index correction is -U_s q^(s-1)/(2(s-2)!). A marked edge has weight X^(F_i+F_(i+1))=X^F_(i+2), so the sum over edges is q A_s+O_s(1). Two distinct edges impose two independent adjacency requirements even if they overlap, hence all multiple-edge corrections are O_s(q^(s-2)); for s=2 there are no such configurations. Excluding the marked vertices from the other selections changes only this error. The resulting additional coefficient is -T_(s,s-1)/(s-2)! as stated. Appending a bounded partial period changes at most O_s(L^(s-1)) index subsets, so the density extends off full blocks. For s=2–5 the determinant of P vanishes in the truncation since h>s, and Cayley–Hamilton gives P^q=(tr P)^(q-1)P for q>=1, justifying exact polynomial interpolation. value.rationale: The theorem resolves a natural conditional divisibility problem for sparse Fibonacci expansions, with limiting bias both above and below 1/s and an explicit finite-length correction that measures adjacency. The exact block counts determine more than the overlapping two-term asymptotic, and a generic transfer formalism on its own supplies neither the arithmetic coefficients nor the valid-from-first-block formulas.
